claims.text: Conventional single-phase ZrB2 requires sintering above 2300 °C.
Conventionally sintered ZrB2 has a porous microstructure with residual microporosity.
Adding a trace amount of Si and using SPS at approximately 2000 °C will lower the required ZrB2 processing temperature.
The Si additive will induce a transient liquid phase during sintering.
Si lowers the local melting point at ZrB2 particle contacts.
The Si-induced liquid phase promotes particle rearrangement and coalescence.
Reactive liquid-phase reactions accelerate ZrB2 sintering and densification at lower temperatures.
The Si/SPS route will reduce microporosity relative to conventional ZrB2 processing.
The Si/SPS route is expected to produce fully densified ZrB2 at approximately 2000 °C.
Reduced porosity will improve the mechanical strength and integrity of ZrB2.
Reduced porosity will improve resistance to degradation during corrosive service.
Si/SPS-processed ZrB2 will exhibit less hole formation during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure than conventionally sintered ZrB2.
Si/SPS-processed ZrB2 will have a lower propensity for premature component failure during prolonged liquid plating-bath exposure.
Conventionally prepared ZrB2 has compromised mechanical integrity under prolonged corrosive conditions.
The preparation boundary compares Si-aided SPS at approximately 2000 °C with conventional sintering above 2300 °C.
The service boundary is extended exposure to a liquid plating bath under identical controlled conditions.
Relative density, porosity, mechanical strength, hole formation, weight loss, and post-exposure microstructural degradation will be measured.
The hypothesis is falsified if the Si/SPS samples show no statistically significant improvement in densification, strength, or resistance to hole formation relative to conventional samples.
